header: Questions operations managers ask in week two
lead: You don't need this on a first read. It's here because someone always asks before signing.

entries.title: How are working-time rules kept up to date?
entries.bodytext:
The rule set covers Austrian and German law on maximum daily and weekly hours, rest between shifts, night work and workers under 18. When the law changes, we update the rules and name the changed rule in the release note.

Rules from your own company agreement are set up per organisation, and updates never overwrite them. Examples are a longer minimum rest, a limit on consecutive closing shifts or a branch that must never be staffed by one person.

entries.title: What happens when the tablet has no network?
entries.bodytext: The clock-in app keeps working offline. It stores each punch on the device with a signed timestamp and sends it when the connection returns, usually within seconds. The audit trail marks late punches but does not treat them as corrections.

entries.title: Can two managers plan one week at once?
entries.bodytext: Yes. Changes are saved per shift, not per week. A shift that someone else is editing is shown as locked, with their name on it. This stops two managers from filling the same Saturday gap, without any check-out or merge step.

entries.title: Who can see an individual's recorded hours?
entries.bodytext: The employee, their direct manager and anyone with the payroll role. Nobody else. Area managers see branch totals, not individual hours, unless they are also someone's direct manager. Every view of a person's record is logged, and the works council can see the log on request.
